source.title: “BNN - BN = ?”: Training Binary Neural Networks without Batch Normalization
source.authors: Tian-Long Chen; Zhenyu (Allen) Zhang; Xu Ouyang; Ze-Chun Liu; Zhiqiang Shen; Zhang-Yang Wang

record.tranche_reason: Compares batch-normalized, unnormalized, and custom BN-Free binary networks and reports classification accuracy and training curves; it does not reproduce the cited BN speed or learning-rate-tolerance measurements.
record.gate_note: Reports test-accuracy tables and curves, not training classification error. Table values are final test accuracies; the text also describes CIFAR-10 ReActNet training curves as nearly overlapping the BN curves. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study extends normalization comparisons to binary networks. Section 4.2 explicitly reports nearly overlapping accuracy-versus-epoch curves for BN-Free and BN ReActNet on CIFAR-10 in both training stages. This qualitative result bears on V6's training-speed component; numerical time-to-accuracy measurements are not required.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their combined BN-Free recipe enables binary-network training without BN while maintaining competitive accuracy and improving stability. Accuracy recovery varies by backbone; hardware speed and energy savings remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses binary neural networks and a custom BN-Free recipe with adaptive gradient clipping, scaled weight standardization, and specialized blocks; reports test accuracy rather than training error or BN-enabled speed and learning-rate tolerance.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, backbone, and AGC clipping threshold affect reported test accuracy; CIFAR-10 results are described as less sensitive to clipping values than CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: Final test and validation accuracies compare BN, naive BN removal, and the proposed BN-Free recipe; ablations measure final accuracy changes from clipping and architectural components.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing BN reduces final classification accuracy in these binary networks, while the proposed replacement recipe recovers accuracy to a backbone-dependent extent.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation, gradient, and latent-weight histograms differ across normalization recipes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The BN-Free recipe concentrates activation and gradient distributions and produces more zero-centered latent weights.

record.peer_reviewed: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The reported main accuracy outcomes are test accuracy, not training error. The training curves are figures without tabulated values, and the text gives only a qualitative comparison for CIFAR-10 ReActNet curves. Several ImageNet comparator accuracies are collected from original papers.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows retained: final test-accuracy values do not measure the training behavior named by the versions, and the qualitative CIFAR-10 curve comparison does not provide separately attributable numerical speed outcomes. Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, Table 4, and Figures 3–6.

untested.parts: Training classification error, near-zero training error, corrupted labels, and effects of model size or early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and excess student width.
Depth-dependent training degradation, shortcut comparisons, and Fixup training.
Comparative initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth.
Stability thresholds, catapult dynamics, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Higher learning-rate tolerance, wall-clock acceleration, and Fixup specifically. The supplied text does not establish comparable accuracy-gain speed across all other backbones and datasets.

missing.what: A qualitative V6 comparison recording nearly overlapping BN-Free and BN accuracy-versus-epoch curves for both CIFAR-10 ReActNet backbones and both training stages. Although rows_left_out declares this exclusion, its requirement for numerical speed outcomes is too restrictive.
missing.locator: Section 4.2, final bullet under CIFAR results; Figure 4

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative curve comparison supports a conditional scope qualification, not an isolated causal estimate of BN's speed benefit. BN-Free changes several components simultaneously. Final accuracy alone does not establish training speed or near-zero training error, and ImageNet BN comparator accuracies in Table 1 are collected from prior papers.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, zero or near-zero training error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects in plain networks and identity shortcuts; the study uses residual BNN architectures but does not compare depths or shortcuts.
Learning rates above the stability limit, loss rises, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.

Higher learning-rate tolerance. The study reports test accuracy tables and describes CIFAR-10 ReActNet curves as nearly overlapping, but does not report separately attributable numerical speed-of-accuracy-gain outcomes.

relationships.condition: ReActNet-18 and ReActNet-A on CIFAR-10, using adaptive gradient clipping, scaled weight standardization, and specialized blocks
relationships.reason: Section 4.2 explicitly describes BN-Free and BN accuracy curves as nearly overlapping in both training stages, qualifying the need for BN to obtain comparable accuracy gain per epoch when replacement techniques are allowed. This verdict rests on the text accompanying Figure 4; no extracted row records it.
relationships.display_finding: BN-Free and batch-normalized accuracy curves nearly overlapped in both training stages when replacement techniques were used.
